title: The Pythagorean Identity
short: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, and finding one value from another.
trouble: Students find the size of cos θ but forget to choose its sign from the quadrant.

blocks.html: Every point $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$ lies on the unit circle, and the unit circle has the equation $x^2 + y^2 = 1$. Put those two facts together and you get the most used identity in trigonometry.

$$\role[y-coordinate squared]{output}{\sin^2\theta} + \role[x-coordinate squared]{input}{\cos^2\theta} = 1 \quad \text{for every angle } \theta.$$ To find one value from the other, solve for its square, take the square root, and choose the sign from the quadrant.

Substitute $x = \cos\theta$ and $y = \sin\theta$ into $x^2 + y^2 = 1$. It is the Pythagorean theorem for the right triangle with hypotenuse $1$ inside the circle. Dividing the identity by $\cos^2\theta$ gives a second form, $\tan^2\theta + 1 = \sec^2\theta$; dividing by $\sin^2\theta$ gives $1 + \cot^2\theta = \csc^2\theta$.
$\sin^2\theta$ means $(\sin\theta)^2$: find the sine, then square it.

blocks.name: unitcircle
blocks.cap: Wherever you turn, the blue and red segments are the legs of a right triangle with hypotenuse $1$.

blocks.title: A rational answer
blocks.q: $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant II. Find $\cos\theta$.
steps: In Quadrant II, $x < 0$, so cosine is negative.

blocks.title: Starting from tangent
blocks.q: $\tan\theta = 2$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant III. Find $\sec\theta$.
steps: In Quadrant III cosine is negative, and secant has the same sign as cosine.

blocks.html: Finding the right size and forgetting the sign: the square root only tells you $\pm$. Always ask where the angle is. A quick sketch of the terminal side shows whether $x$ (cosine) and $y$ (sine) are positive or negative.
